text:
Simon Nemec is Calgary's new long-term bet on the blue line. The second pick of the 2022 draft came over from New Jersey, and Flames Nation reported on Nov. 5 that he signed a five-year deal at $7.25 million a year. With Kevin Bahl hurt, Sportsnet and others have the spotlight on him now, and he's already playing over 21 minutes a night.

His start reads worse than it is. No goals in 18 games on 2.75 expected goals is the definition of due, and the Flames have scored 4.6 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. His seven assists are a fair return. The concern is the chances against: Calgary takes only 46% of the expected goals with him at five on five, even while out-shooting teams (52.5% of attempts). The tools say that should improve. He's fast (90th percentile top speed by NHL Edge), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 18% of entries at his own blue line last season (typical 11%) and carrying the puck in on 48% of his own. Evolving-Hockey had him 72nd of 215 defencemen in 2025-26. The first goal is coming.
